en.title: Tucker Carlson Roasts Blockbusters on SNL's 'Weekend Update'
en.summary: Jeremy Culhane brought back his popular Tucker Carlson impression on 'Saturday Night Live' Season 52. The comedian offered his unique take on summer's biggest films during 'Weekend Update.'
en.body:
The first 'Weekend Update' segment of 'Saturday Night Live' Season 52 saw the much-anticipated return of **Jeremy Culhane**'s impression of polarizing political commentator **Tucker Carlson**. Stepping into the role once more, Culhane delivered a fictional review of some of the summer's most talked-about blockbusters, offering his signature blend of outrage and bewildered commentary.

Carlson's review touched upon several high-profile releases, including a fictionalized take on 'The Odyssey,' a gender-neutral 'Spider-Man,' and a film described as 'left-wing 'Obsession'.' Culhane, as Carlson, wryly commented on the IMAX 70mm format used for 'The Odyssey,' quipping about the 'Hollywood cabal' and its choice of film stock. The sketch also included a jab at Paramount+, poking fun at the streaming service's perceived struggles. The fictional reviews, while not based on actual film content or release details, provided a comedic lens through which to examine contemporary filmmaking trends and the cultural discourse surrounding them.

## A Comedic Take on Summer's Biggest Films

The 'Weekend Update' segment has long served as 'SNL's' primary vehicle for topical humor and political satire, and Culhane's impression of Carlson has become a fan favorite. By placing Carlson in the unlikely role of a film critic, the sketch aimed to satirize both the commentator's outspoken style and the often-intense reactions to major movie releases. The choice to review films like 'The Odyssey' and a hypothetical 'gender-neutral Spider-Man' allowed for commentary on themes of representation and artistic direction, filtered through the exaggerated persona of Carlson. The inclusion of 'left-wing 'Obsession'' further leaned into political commentary, suggesting a critique of perceived liberal agendas within Hollywood productions. This approach allows 'SNL' to engage with cultural conversations without directly addressing the real-world figures or films, offering a layer of comedic distance.

## Fan and Community Reaction

Fans of 'Saturday Night Live' and those familiar with **Tucker Carlson**'s public persona likely found the sketch particularly amusing. The impression itself has garnered significant attention, with many viewers praising Culhane's ability to capture Carlson's distinctive mannerisms and vocal inflections. The segment tapped into the ongoing cultural conversations surrounding media representation and political commentary in entertainment. For viewers who follow both pop culture and political news, the juxtaposition of Carlson's conservative viewpoints with critiques of modern blockbusters provided a unique comedic experience. The widespread sharing of clips and discussions online indicates a strong audience resonance with this type of satirical content, highlighting the sketch's success in generating buzz and commentary within the fan community.

## What's Next

While the specific films reviewed were fictional creations for the sketch, 'Saturday Night Live' continues its 52nd season with new episodes airing weekly on NBC. Viewers can anticipate further topical humor and celebrity impressions as the season progresses, with potential for other fan-favorite characters to return.
